title: Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
plain: The transmission computer found a problem and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light. This code is a messenger: the real fault is stored as a separate code in the transmission computer.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Transmission may be stuck in one gear (limp mode)
Harsh, late or erratic shifting
Other transmission warning lights or messages

causes.name: Another transmission fault stored in the transmission computer
Faulty transmission sensor or shift solenoid
Low or burnt transmission fluid
Wiring or connector problem at the transmission
Faulty transmission control module

checks: Use a scanner that can read transmission module codes, not just engine codes
Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Inspect the wiring and connectors at the transmission and its computer
fix: Read the codes stored in the transmission computer and repair that fault. P0700 itself clears once the underlying problem is fixed.
examples: Usually shows up together with a second transmission code that points to the real problem

title: Transmission Control System Range/Performance
plain: The transmission computer sees that the transmission control system is not behaving the way it expects, even though no single circuit has failed outright.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Rough or unusual shifting
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low or degraded transmission fluid
Transmission control module software or internal fault
Poor power or ground supply to the transmission computer

checks: Check for other transmission codes and fix those first
Check fluid level and condition
Check for software updates for the transmission computer
fix: Fix any related codes and fluid problems first; a computer reflash or replacement is needed only after power, ground and wiring check out.

title: Transmission Control System Electrical
plain: The transmission computer has detected an electrical problem in the transmission control system, such as a bad power feed, ground or internal circuit.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode)
Harsh or no shifting

causes.name: Poor power or ground to the transmission computer
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the transmission
Failed transmission control module

checks: Check battery voltage and the fuses that feed the transmission computer
Inspect transmission wiring and grounds for corrosion or damage
fix: Repair the power, ground or wiring fault; replace and program the transmission computer only if it has failed internally.

title: Torque Converter/Brake Switch B Circuit
plain: There's a problem with the brake pedal switch signal the transmission uses to know when you're braking. It's important because the same switch runs your brake lights.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Brake lights may stay on or not work
Torque converter may not unlock when stopping, causing a stall or shudder
Cruise control may not work

causes.name: Faulty or misadjusted brake pedal switch
Blown fuse for the brake light circuit
Damaged wiring or connector at the brake switch
Burned-out brake bulbs on some models

checks: Have someone confirm the brake lights come on and go off with the pedal
Check the brake light fuse
Inspect and test the brake pedal switch and its connector
fix: Most often a new or readjusted brake pedal switch, or repair of a fuse or wiring fault in that circuit.

title: Clutch Switch Input Circuit Malfunction
plain: On a manual-transmission car, the computer isn't getting a sensible signal from the switch that tells it when the clutch pedal is pressed.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Car may not start, or starts without the clutch pressed
Cruise control may not work or not cancel

causes.name: Faulty or misadjusted clutch pedal switch
Damaged wiring or connector at the clutch switch
Broken switch mounting or bumper on the clutch pedal

checks: Check that the switch is in place and touched by the pedal
Test the switch for on and off as the pedal moves
fix: Usually a new or readjusted clutch pedal switch, or a wiring repair.

title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit (PRNDL Input)
plain: The computer isn't getting a good signal from the sensor that tells it which gear the shifter is in (Park, Reverse, Neutral, Drive).
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not start in Park or Neutral, or may start in gear
Gear indicator on the dash may be wrong or blank
Harsh or wrong shifting, or limp mode
Reverse lights may not work

causes.name: Faulty transmission range sensor (neutral safety switch)
Range sensor out of adjustment
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the sensor
Worn or misadjusted shift cable or linkage
Faulty transmission computer

checks: Check that the shifter lines up with the gear shown on the dash
Inspect the range sensor connector for water, corrosion or damage
Check the range sensor readings with a scanner while moving through each gear
fix: Usually adjusting or replacing the transmission range sensor, or repairing its wiring or the shift linkage.
examples: Often seen on older Ford trucks and SUVs, where the range sensor sits outside the transmission and is exposed to water and dirt

title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit
plain: There's a problem in the circuit for the sensor that measures how much fluid is in the transmission.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Low fluid warning may show even when fluid is fine
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Faulty transmission fluid level sensor
Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Actual fluid level too low or too high
Transmission computer fault

checks: Check the actual fluid level using the maker's procedure
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector
fix: Confirm the true fluid level first, then repair the wiring or replace the fluid level sensor.

title: Transmission Fluid Level Too Low
plain: The computer thinks there isn't enough fluid in the transmission. Driving low on fluid can quickly damage the transmission.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Slipping or delayed shifts
Fluid spots under the car

causes.name: Transmission fluid leak
Fluid not refilled correctly after a service
Faulty fluid level sensor or wiring

checks: Check the fluid level the way the maker specifies (many need the engine running and fluid at a set temperature)
Look for leaks at the pan, lines, cooler and seals
fix: Fix any leak and fill to the correct level with the right fluid; replace the level sensor only if the fluid level is actually correct.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit
plain: There's a problem in the circuit for the sensor that tells the computer how hot the transmission fluid is.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Harsh or late shifts, especially when cold
Torque converter may not lock up, hurting fuel economy

causes.name: Faulty transmission fluid temperature sensor
Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Fluid actually overheating from low fluid or heavy towing

checks: Compare the transmission temperature reading to engine coolant temperature on a cold start
Check fluid level and condition
Inspect the transmission connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new fluid temperature sensor (on many models part of the internal wiring harness) or a wiring repair.

title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit
plain: The computer isn't getting a good signal from the sensor that measures how fast the transmission's input shaft is spinning, so it can't shift properly.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode)
Speedometer may act up on some models

causes.name: Faulty input/turbine speed sensor
Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Low or dirty transmission fluid
Metal debris on the sensor tip
Transmission computer fault

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring for damage or oil
Check fluid level and condition
Watch input speed on a scanner while driving to see if the signal drops out
fix: Most often a new input speed sensor or a wiring repair; on some models the sensor is inside the transmission.
examples: Frequently reported on Dodge Caravan and Chrysler Town and Country minivans

checks: Test whether the mode button changes the dash indicator
Inspect the switch and its wiring at the shifter or dash
fix: Usually a new mode switch or a wiring repair.

title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer isn't getting a good signal from the sensor that measures how fast the transmission's output shaft (and so the wheels) is turning.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Speedometer may stop working or jump around
Harsh or erratic shifts, or limp mode
ABS or traction control light may come on in some vehicles

causes.name: Faulty output shaft speed sensor
Damaged wiring or connector to the sensor
Metal debris on the sensor tip
Damaged reluctor (tone) ring
Transmission computer fault

checks: Check whether the speedometer works
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Pull the sensor and check its tip for metal debris
fix: Most often a new output speed sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Engine Speed Input Circuit
plain: The transmission computer isn't getting a good engine speed (RPM) signal, which it needs to time shifts.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Harsh or erratic shifting
Tachometer may act up

causes.name: Faulty crankshaft position sensor
Damaged wiring between the engine and transmission computers
Network or computer communication fault

checks: Check for crankshaft sensor or network codes and fix those first
Inspect the wiring and connectors between the computers
fix: Usually a crankshaft position sensor or a wiring repair, depending on where the signal is lost.
